rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->A message from [enclaveFaction_name], relayed three times through droids who do not trust radio. It is short, and it is not a request yet.

Nobody on this world makes droids. [hiveFaction_name] know how: the factory patterns sit in their databases, left there by the company that bought them and then walked away. But they are workers left behind at a factory, not a whole people, and they cannot run the line they remember.

[enclaveFaction_name] are escaped droids. They mend each other and nothing else. Every one of them that falls stays fallen.

The two are allies, and neither can do this alone. Neither will let the other hold it. The Jawa fix droids for anyone, and belong to neither. If you answer, they will come to you, one step at a time.

li.label: The Unbolting of the Line
li.text:
The first frame off the line was carried to the Rust Cathedral by six droids who would not let anyone else touch it. There [enclaveFaction_name] fitted it with a salvaged head, as they fit every one of their own, and took the bolt off before it ever woke.
Forty-one fell. Today one stood up.
[hiveFaction_name] sent no one to the rite. Their queen sent one sentence instead: the work is being finished. For the Hive there is no higher praise.
The Enclaves have opened their droid-construction teaching to the Jawa. What you build with it is born free.

li.label: The line stays unfinished
li.text: [enclaveFaction_name] have stopped sending messages about the line. Nobody blames anyone out loud. The patterns stay in [hiveFaction_name]'s databases, and the fallen stay fallen.

li.label: Nothing they freed comes back
li.text:
The Empire's shuttle was not even out of the sky before [hiveFaction_name] knew. [enclaveFaction_name] knew an hour later, from the Hive.
The patterns were the Hive's memory, and the line was the Enclaves' only way to stop counting their dead. The Jawa sold both for silver. Neither people will forget it, and nothing they freed comes back.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->A protocol droid from [settlement_label] is walking three of [enclaveFaction_name]'s fallen across the flats to your shop. It has asked you to listen to one sentence before you decide.

"Forty-one of us fell this year. None were replaced. None can be."

The three it brings are not beyond saving, only beyond the Enclaves' own hands. They will stay with you for [jobTicks_duration]. Fit each of them a part at a repair bench.

They are not paying for the work; they are paying back the parts, [payHonest_money] a droid for a standard part, [payFine_money] for a better one, [payShoddy_money] for a worn one. The Enclaves will judge the job by the worst of the three that walks out.

li.customLetterLabel: The Count: three of the fallen
li.customLetterText: [lodgers0_nameDef] and two others came in carried as much as walking. The protocol droid that brought them did not come in. It said it would be back in [jobTicks_duration], and that it was counting.\n\nOpen each panel at a repair bench and fit a part. Which parts is your business; the Enclaves will see what walks out.

li.label: The Count: they remember the parts
li.text: The three walked out on better parts than the Enclaves have fitted anyone in years. The protocol droid ran a diagnostic on each, twice, and logged the result to [enclaveFaction_name] before it said anything to you.\n\nThen it gave you a second message, from the First Speaker, R-41 Rell. [hiveFaction_name] hold the patterns for making bodies. Would the Jawa carry the Enclaves' word to them?

li.label: The Count: three walk home
li.text: The three walked out straight and cycling clean. The protocol droid counted them, and then counted them again.\n\nIt carried a second message, from the First Speaker, R-41 Rell. [hiveFaction_name] hold the patterns for making bodies. Would the Jawa carry the Enclaves' word to them?

li.label: The Count: they walk, on worn parts
li.text: The three walk. At least one of them walks the way scrap walks. The protocol droid logged every part number before it left, and said nothing about them.\n\nIt still carried the First Speaker's message, because there is nobody else to carry it to. [hiveFaction_name] hold the patterns for making bodies. Would the Jawa carry the Enclaves' word to them?

li.label: The Count: nothing changed
li.text: The protocol droid collected the three as they came in. It did not ask why. The count stands where it stood.

li.label: The Count: one more fallen
li.text: [enclaveFaction_name] brought you their fallen and you kept one. They have a word for what you are now, and they will use it.

li.label: The Count: forty-two
li.text: One of the three did not survive your shop. The protocol droid updated its count in front of you.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->[enclaveFaction_name] have carried their word to [hiveFaction_name], and the Hive has answered the only way it knows: it will send someone to watch.
Two of the Hive's overseers, a foundry engineer and one of the aristocrats who compete for the queen's notice, will stay at your colony for [stayTicks_duration] under the guard of two Enclave security droids. The Hive will not give its patterns to hands it has not seen work. The Enclaves will not let organics hold a droid factory alone. You are the hands in the middle.
Accept, and the Enclaves broker a truce: the Hive will hold off its raids for as long as this work goes on. Harm a guest, and there is no truce and no line.

li.customLetterText:
[envoys0_nameDef] and another overseer of [hiveFaction_name] have arrived, walked in between two of [enclaveFaction_name]'s security droids. They will stay [stayTicks_duration], and they will watch everything.
The Hive holds off its raids while the truce lasts. Keep your guests whole.

li.label: The Envoy: the Hive has seen enough
li.text:
The overseers leave as they came, between the Enclave droids. Before she goes, the foundry engineer says what the Hive needs, as if it were obvious: the three pattern cores, still sealed where the company left them. Without them the patterns in the Hive's databases are only memory.
[hiveFaction_name] think better of you. So, a little, do [enclaveFaction_name].

li.label: The Envoy: the truce is broken
li.text: A guest of the line died at your colony. [hiveFaction_name] do not ask how. The truce is over, and the line will not be built through you.

li.label: The Envoy: a guest in chains
li.text: You arrested a guest of the line. [hiveFaction_name] and [enclaveFaction_name] heard the same thing at the same moment. The truce is over, and so is the line.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->[hiveFaction_name]'s foundry engineer has told the Jawa what the Hive never told anyone: the three pattern cores are still sealed in the fabrication hall of the old silicax foundry, the company site both [hiveFaction_name] and [enclaveFaction_name] fled when it collapsed.

The Hive cannot go back. Its queen does not move, and its workers will not leave her. The Enclaves will not walk into a factory. The Jawa will.

Droids the company left behind still walk the ruin, gone wild in the dark. Bring them down however you like. Any you capture and release without a restraining bolt will walk to the Enclaves, and the Enclaves will remember it.

Bring all three cores home within [coreTicks_duration]. Then [enclaveFaction_name] will send for them.

li.label: The Pattern Cores: too long
li.text: [enclaveFaction_name] have stopped asking after the cores. [hiveFaction_name] say nothing at all. The ruin keeps them a while longer.

li.label: The Pattern Cores: one is gone
li.text: A pattern core was destroyed. The patterns it held are gone with it, and the other two are only part of a memory.

li.label: The Pattern Cores: carried home
li.text: An Enclave courier came for the three cores, a hauling droid with an escort that did not take its eyes off the horizon. It signed for each core twice, once for [enclaveFaction_name] and once for [hiveFaction_name].\n\nThe patterns and the means to read them are in one place again for the first time since the company left.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->The patterns and the cores are in one place again, and still nothing is being built. [hiveFaction_name] have the knowledge and not the means: the company took its stockpiles when it left, and the Hive's workers are too few to run a line that was built for thousands. [enclaveFaction_name] have hands that have never built anything.

So the line asks the Jawa for both. An Enclave shuttle will land at your colony and wait [titheTicks_duration] to be loaded with the tithe: [titheText]. It will also carry [handsAsk], who will work the line beside the droids for [lendTicks_duration] before coming home.

The shuttle leaves as soon as it holds both.
handsAsk(minCrafting>0)->one colonist with Crafting [minCrafting] or better

li.label: The Tithe: the shuttle has landed
li.text: [enclaveFaction_name]'s shuttle has landed. It waits for the tithe, [titheText], and for one crafter to work the line. It leaves the moment it holds both, or in [titheTicks_duration] if it never does.

li.label: The Tithe: the shuttle left empty
li.text: The Enclave shuttle waited as long as it was told to, and left with nothing. [hiveFaction_name] will not say what they think of that. The line stands idle a while longer.

li.label: The Tithe: the shuttle is gone
li.text: The shuttle [enclaveFaction_name] sent for the tithe was destroyed at your colony. They will send another when they have one to send.

li.label: The Tithe: paid
li.text: The shuttle lifted heavy. The tithe is on its way to the line, and so is your crafter, who will work beside [enclaveFaction_name]'s droids and under [lendFaction_name]'s overseers for [lendTicks_duration].\n\nNeither people has ever worked one line with the other. Now they will have to.

li.label: The Hands: the line is assembled
li.text: {PAWNS} came home from the line, quieter than they left and a much better crafter for it.\n\nThe line is assembled. [hiveFaction_name] and [enclaveFaction_name] worked it together for ten days and nobody died of it. The first run is next.

li.label: The Hands: lost on the line
li.text: The crafter you lent to the line died there. [lendFaction_name] sent the body home. [hiveFaction_name] and [enclaveFaction_name] blame each other, and both of them blame the line. The work stops until someone is willing to try again.

rulesStrings.li:
questDescription->The line is ready. [enclaveFaction_name] and [hiveFaction_name] mean to run it for the first time, and the first run will light the sky over the foundry for [runTicks_duration].

Everyone knows what that means. A light like that is seen from orbit, and [enemyFaction_name] has not forgotten the Geonosians who built its battle station. It will want to know who built this. The answer is the Jawa.

Accept, and the run begins. Hold your colony until the run is done and the strike is broken. If the strike still holds your colony [holdTicks_duration] after the run ends, the first run counts for nothing.

li.customLetterText: [enemyFaction_name] saw the light. A strike force is coming for the Jawa who built the line.\n\nHold until the run is done and the strike is broken.

li.label: First Light: the run is done
li.text: The foundry has gone dark again. The first run is finished: frames on the floor that no hand on this world has made in a generation. [enclaveFaction_name] are counting them twice.

li.inspectString: The strike must be broken within: {0}

li.label: First Light: the run counts for nothing
li.text: [enemyFaction_name] still holds your colony. The frames from the first run were scattered to hiding before anyone could fit a head to one. [enclaveFaction_name] will try again, when they can.

li.label: First Light: held
li.text: The strike is broken and the run is done. [enclaveFaction_name] are already carrying the first frame away.
